READING_COMPREHENSION.readingText: At a special sports day, a group of students and a friendly robot try different sports. The students can run and play ball games, but they can't fly. The robot can do gymnastics and karate, and it can skateboard very well. One student can run fast but can't play tennis. Everyone discovers that people have different abilities.

questions.q: What sports can the robot do?

READING_COMPREHENSION.readingText: Nina and Theo plan a picnic after a morning at the sports centre. Nina loves making sandwiches, but Theo can't stand cutting tomatoes. Theo likes taking photos and Nina likes cycling in the park. They both hate sitting indoors on sunny days, so they take their food outside and have a picnic.

options: The sports hall is a kitchen

READING_COMPREHENSION.category: Sport - A New Friend at the Club
READING_COMPREHENSION.readingText: Freya meets Jun at a sports club. Freya's favourite sport is basketball, and she can play very well. She plays twice a week at the school sports hall. Jun prefers swimming. He swims on Saturdays at a pool near his school. His brother also likes swimming, so they sometimes practise together.

questions.a: At a pool near his school
options: At a pool near his school

READING_COMPREHENSION.category: Culture and Skills - Sports for All
READING_COMPREHENSION.readingText: Teenagers can do many sports at school. Indoor activities take place in sports halls, while outdoor sports are often played on fields. Different groups of students may prefer different sports, but everyone should have equal opportunities to take part. Sport is also shown in the media, and balanced coverage can help young people see many different sporting heroes.

questions.q: Where do indoor sports take place?
Where are many outdoor sports played?
Why is balanced media coverage useful?
questions.a: It shows many different sporting heroes
options: It shows many different sporting heroes

READING_COMPREHENSION.readingText: Camila Torres is a young athlete from South America. Her main event is the long jump. She trains five days a week and can jump very far. She has two national medals and one international medal. Camila also visits schools and talks to students about sport, practice and confidence.

questions.q: What does she do at schools?
questions.a: She talks to students about sport and confidence
options: She talks to students about sport and confidence

READING_COMPREHENSION.category: Culture and Skills - Unusual Free Time
READING_COMPREHENSION.readingText: Three teenagers have unusual hobbies. Alex makes tiny sculptures from soap. The hobby is inexpensive, but he needs a small tool and a lot of patience. Jess practises parkour. She can run, jump and climb very well, but she says people must understand their limits and be in good physical condition. Ben plays a digital version of a traditional musical instrument because it is easier for him to use.

questions.q: What does Jess say is important?
questions.a: Understanding your limits and being fit
options: Understanding your limits and being fit

questions.a: A digital version of an instrument
options: A digital version of an instrument

READING_COMPREHENSION.readingText: Leo and Maya have different opinions about sport. Leo loves football and thinks it is exciting. Maya doesn't agree; she finds football a little boring, but she loves cycling. Leo thinks cycling is difficult, while Maya says it is relaxing and fun. They both like swimming and go to the pool together once a week.

questions.q: What does Maya think about football?
What sport do they both like?

READING_COMPREHENSION.readingText: A school sports club wants everyone to feel welcome. Boys and girls can join the same training sessions, and students choose sports because they enjoy them, not because a sport is 'for boys' or 'for girls'. The club also puts photos of male and female sporting heroes on its walls. The teachers say respect and equal opportunities make the club stronger.

questions.q: Who can join the training sessions?
What photos are on the walls?
